title: Advanced IAM, Federation & Zero Trust — Failure Injection & Auto-Healing
purpose: Simulates Service Account Key Compromise & Automated Quarantine: detects key leak on GitHub and revokes credentials within 5 seconds.
routing_rationale: Cloud Asset Inventory and Eventarc integrate with secret scanning partners to detect leaked service account keys and automatically disable them before exploitation.

nodes.label: Exposed JSON SA Key
nodes.detail: Developer accidentally committed service-account-key.json to public GitHub repo.

nodes.label: GitHub Secret Scanning
nodes.detail: Identifies Google Cloud private key pattern within 2 seconds of git push.

nodes.label: Eventarc Security Receiver
nodes.detail: Receives key compromise event; routes to automated revocation function.

nodes.label: Cloud Functions Key Revoker
nodes.detail: Calls IAM Admin API to disable leaked key ID in 3.4 seconds.

steps.title: Secret Detection & Ingestion
steps.action: GitHub scans commit, identifies GCP private key, and notifies Google Security webhook.
steps.why_traversal: Catches exposure within seconds before malicious actors can exploit it.

steps.title: Automated Key Deactivation
steps.action: Function disables key immediately and notifies security operations in Slack.
steps.why_traversal: Reduces exposure window from days to under 4 seconds.

scenarios.label: Revoked Key Halts Production Batch Job
scenarios.root_cause: The leaked key was actively shared with a critical production billing batch process.
scenarios.diverted_path: Batch job fails with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
scenarios.recovery: Migrate production batch jobs to Workload Identity Federation, eliminating JSON keys forever.
